name: Oregon
one: Oregon mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Oregon, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

No request needed

There is no request to make: ballots go to every active registered voter. If your ballot has been lost, destroyed or damaged so that you cannot vote it, call your county elections office for a replacement. If My Vote shows your registration as inactive, update it or contact your county, because ballots are not mailed to inactive voters. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, is the last day to return your ballot. Drop boxes and county elections offices take ballots until 8 p.m. A ballot sent by mail must be postmarked by Election Day, and is counted if it reaches the county elections office up to 7 days after (by Tuesday, November 10, 2026). The state recommends mailing by Tuesday, October 27; after that, ask a post office worker to postmark it by hand. (official page)

Ask for a ballot online, on Oregon’s own site

At school away from home, in Oregon or in another state? What Oregon says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Oregon votes entirely by mail: every active registered voter is mailed a ballot. Counties began mailing ballots for the November 3, 2026 election on October 14. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. You do not need to ask for a ballot. If you will be away from your home address (for example at college out of state, or traveling), update your mailing address in My Vote so your ballot is sent there. A ballot can be sent to you anywhere in the world. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Or fill out the Absentee Ballot Request Form (SEL 111) and return it to your county elections office. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • Drop box. Put it in any official ballot drop box in Oregon by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The state strongly encourages drop boxes. The Ballot Drop Box Locator shows places and hours. (official page)
  • By mail. Mail it so it is postmarked by Election Day. Mailing by October 27 is recommended because delivery times vary. (official page)
  • In person. Take it to your county elections office by 8 p.m. on Election Day (offices are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. that day). Someone can return your ballot for you; they must put it in a drop box or the mail within 2 days of getting it, or by Election Day, whichever comes first. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness is needed. You must sign the ballot return envelope yourself; no one else may sign it. The county compares your signature with the ones in your voter record. If it does not match, or you forgot to sign, the county sends you a notice, and you have until 21 days after the election to fix it with your county elections office. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Oregon’s own site (official page)

Students

At school in Oregon, away from home

For students, your residential address (which sets what is on your ballot) can be your parents' or other family home, or where you live as a student. You choose, but only one. Voting residence is not the same as residence for in-state tuition; it is the place you consider home and intend to return to. If you use a campus address, include the dorm and room number; a PO box is not a residential address. Your mailing address, where the ballot is sent, can be different, such as a campus address. (official page)

At school in another state, with Oregon as home

Oregon voters going to college in another state can still get their Oregon ballot: update your mailing address in My Vote, or send the Absentee Ballot Request Form to your county. Students from another state going to school in Oregon may stay registered at home or register at their Oregon school address, but only one; voting in two places is a felony. Students studying abroad can update their mailing address in My Vote. (official page)

Military and overseas

Ballots are mailed to registered military and overseas voters at least 45 days before Election Day, and many can mark their ballot with Oregon's Online Ballot Marking Tool through My Vote. You can return it by mail (received, or mailed with a valid U.S. postmark, by 8 p.m. on Election Day; foreign postmarks do not count), by fax or email (with the Secret Ballot Waiver and signed return envelope), or through an electronic return system where your county offers one. You must be registered at least 21 days before the election. The federal write-in ballot (FWAB) is a backup if your ballot does not arrive. (official page)

Oregon in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Oregon has no separate early in-person voting period on the pages we read; every voter gets a ballot by mail and can return it as soon as it is filled in. Your county elections office can help in person, and replaces lost or damaged ballots.
  • For this election the state also offers free ballot tracking by text, email or phone call (BallotTrax); the sign-up link is on the state's Track Your Ballot page. The state's FAQ notes that a phone number or email given for county ballot tracking becomes a public record.
  • The registration deadline for November 3, 2026 was October 13 (21 days before the election).

How this was checked

  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
